Nordpred age-period-cohort model with a power link

Source: R/model-nordpred.R
nordpred_apc.Rd

The Nordpred method of Møller et al. (2003) for projections of cancer incidence and mortality: an age-period-cohort model for 5-year age groups and 5-year periods, fitted by Poisson maximum likelihood with a power link, whose linear trend (the drift) is projected and damped in later periods. The deaths D of age group a in period p with exposure E are Poisson with mean

Usage

nordpred_apc(
  link = c("power5", "log"),
  n_periods = 4:6,
  recent = NULL,
  cut_trend = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.75),
  est_age = NULL,
  use_age = NULL
)

Arguments

link

"power5" (Nordpred's power link) or "log" (multiplicative Poisson age-period-cohort model).

n_periods

Candidate numbers of 5-year periods in the prediction base, at least 3 each (nordpred's default 4:6). A single number fixes the base.

recent

Project the slope of the last 10 years (TRUE), the average drift (FALSE), or choose by the test described above (NULL).

cut_trend

Proportions of the drift cut in the future 5-year periods.

est_age

Lower bound of the youngest age group in the regression (nordpred's startestage). Default: the first age group of the grid.

use_age

Lower bound of the youngest age group projected with the regression (nordpred's startuseage). Default: est_age.

Value

A model specification.

Details

E (A[a] + d p + P[p] + C[c])^5

(link = "power5"), with age effects A, drift d, non-linear period effects P and cohort effects C (cohort c = p - a on the scale of 5-year steps), or E exp(A[a] + d p + P[p] + C[c]) (link = "log", the multiplicative model). The power 5 levels off the exponential growth of the multiplicative model (Møller et al. 2003). The model is fitted as a generalised linear model with a Poisson variance function and the power link mu^(1/5) on the rates, written for this package.

The specification follows Møller et al. (2003) and the R package nordpred (version 1.1, by Møller and Weedon-Fekjær, GPL-2), whose documentation and code define the details below. This implementation is written independently of nordpred's code. Its point projections agree with those of nordpred on the same data to a relative difference below 1e-7 (see the unit tests).

  • Identification. The period effects of the first and the last period and the cohort effects of the oldest and the youngest cohort are zero, so that the drift carries the linear trend (the identification of nordpred).

  • Prediction base. n_periods lists the candidate numbers of recent 5-year periods to fit. The model is fitted to the largest; while its deviance rejects the fit at the 1% level (chi-squared goodness of fit), the oldest period is dropped, down to the smallest candidate.

  • Trend. With recent = NULL the projected drift is the slope of the last 10 years (the change of the period part of the linear predictor between the last two periods) if a quadratic period term is significant at the 5% level in a Poisson model with log link (age, drift, quadratic term and cohort effects), and the average drift d otherwise.

  • Cut trend. In future period j the drift is multiplied by 1 - cut_trend[j] (cumulated over the periods): the default reduces it by 0%, 25%, 50%, 75% and 75% in the five 5-year periods after the last observation.

  • Cohorts. A future cell keeps the effect of its cohort if that cohort is older than the cohort of age group use_age in the last observed period, and takes the effect of that cohort otherwise.

  • Young ages. Age groups below use_age are projected at the mean of the observed rates of the last two 5-year periods; age groups below est_age do not enter the regression.

Annual data (package-specific). mortensor models work on single calendar years. The deaths and exposures of the training years are summed to 5-year periods that end with the last training year; up to four earlier years that do not fill a 5-year period are left out. The model is fitted and projected on these periods. Annual rates are obtained by linear interpolation of the linear predictor (the fifth root of the rate, or its logarithm with link = "log") between the midpoints of the periods: the fitted value of the last observed period at its midpoint (two years before the last training year) and the projections of the future periods at theirs. Where the linear predictor changes linearly over the periods, its mean over the five years of a future period equals the Nordpred projection of that period. Fitted rates are the fitted period rates in each year of the periods fitted, and missing for earlier years and for age groups below est_age. The age groups must be 5 years wide; the last may be open or wider (it counts as one 5-year step for the cohorts, as nordpred's 85+). Use mt_regroup() or step_regroup() for single years of age.

Uncertainty (package-specific). Nordpred gives point projections and documents no method for prediction intervals. Here each draw takes the coefficients from their asymptotic normal distribution (estimates and the inverse Fisher information of the Poisson model) and projects them as above. Draws describe the uncertainty of the coefficients only, with no variation of future period effects and no overdispersion, so intervals are narrow when the data are large; check coverage in a backtest and widen them with recalibrated() if needed. With the power link, linear predictors below 0.001 of a draw are set to 0.001 (a safeguard). Age groups below use_age have no uncertainty. Predictive draws (mt_forecast(predictive = TRUE)) add Poisson variation of the deaths given the rates.

Beyond five future periods (25 years) the last value of cut_trend is used (nordpred projects at most five periods). The candidate number of periods is chosen with the link of the model (nordpred uses the power link for this choice also when link = "log").

References

Møller B, Fekjær H, Hakulinen T, Sigvaldason H, Storm HH, Talbäck M, Haldorsen T (2003). Prediction of cancer incidence in the Nordic countries: empirical comparison of different approaches. Statistics in Medicine 22(17): 2751-2766. doi:10.1002/sim.1481

Examples

x <- mt_example(deaths = "single", years = 1990:2019)
x5 <- mt_regroup(x, age = seq(30, 85, 5))
fit <- mt_fit(nordpred_apc(), x5)
fc <- mt_forecast(fit, h = 10, n_draws = 100, seed = 1)
